# Introduction 

This document is the user guide of the REST API for Product Usage Management. It includes the data model definition as well as all available operations for the ProductUsage resource.

The Product Usage Management API provides a standardized mechanism for Product Usage management such as the creation, update, retrieval of a Product Usage or of a collection of Product Usage.

A Product Usage entity represents the structured report of a service that has been delivered, guided to a product, used and is considered billable. Each Product Usage entity is defined by a corresponding Product Usage Specification, which standardizes what type of usage occurred (e.g., voice, data session, API call) and its associated characteristics (e.g., duration, data consumption, correlation identifier). The main content of a Product Usage is a list of characteristics (name-value pairs), that are needed to guide and/or to rate the usage. For example, A and B numbers in a telephone call, amount of data transferred in a data packet transfer, etc. Other key attributes of Product Usage are its id, creation date, status and the id of the related product and of the related Product Usage Specification.

TMF767 Product Usage Catalog Management API is responsible for managing Product Usage Specifications that represents a catalog view of the targeted Product Usage comprised of characteristics specifications which define all the attributes known for the particular usage.

The Product Usage API manages both rated and non-rated usages. For example, it allows a service provider:

- To retrieve usage generated by a partner platform in order to rate it
- To provide rated usages to a partner for their consumption

A ProductUsage represents an entity that may be of interest to the business and can have charges applied to it. It is comprised of characteristics which define all the attributes known for that particular type of usage. The main attributes are its id, creationDate, usageType, related UsageSpecification, characteristics (name/value pairs), status, price charged (date, amount, taxes), product involved in the usage. A ProductUsage follows a simple life cycle which is presented in the following chapter 'ProductUsage life cycle'.

The Product Usage API exposes the following operations on the ProductUsage resource:

- Creation of a ProductUsage. Note that creation of a ProductUsage can be done without the API, rather as the result of internal processing by an online charging system or policy control system
- Retrieval of a ProductUsage or a collection of ProductUsage, depending on filter criteria
- Partial update of a ProductUsage or of a collection of ProductUsage
- Deletion of a ProductUsage

The Product Usage API also optionally exposes the ExportJob resource:

- An ExportJob represents a task used to export productUsage representations.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- To trigger the export of productUsage, an ExportJob is created by the API client using POST operation on the ExportJob resource.
- The ExportJob is then processed by the API server, which generates a file containing the productUsage representations and stores it in a designated location.
- The API client can then retrieve the ExportJob status and the generated file using the GET operation on the ExportJob resource.
- The ExportJob can be used to export productUsage representations in various formats, such as JSON or CSV.
- The ExportJob resource allows the API client to specify the filter criteria for the productUsage representations to be exported, such as creationDate range, status, related product.id.
- An ExportJob follows a simple life cycle which is presented in the following chapter 'ExportJob life cycle'.

The Product Usage API exposes the following operations on the ExportJob resource:

- Creation of an ExportJob
- Retrieval of an ExportJob or a collection of ExportJob, depending on filter criteria
- Deletion of an ExportJob

| initialized | This acknowledges that the ProductUsage hasbeen initialized and is pending validation |
| --- | --- |
| rejected | The rejected state is where invalid information isprovided through the ProductUsage instance (notnecessarily checked synchronously) |
| validated | The product, customer billing account and pricingrules used to rate the ProductUsage have beenfound |
| rated | The ProductUsage has been rated, at least oneproduct price has been created(usageProductPrice) within the ProductUsage |
| corrected | The ProductUsage is resubmitted after errorcorrection |
| superseded | This ProductUsage record has been supersededby another due to error (e.g., wrong price) and isno longer billable |
| notRated | The ProductUsage has not been rated, due tobusiness rules (e.g., no price applicable for thisusage type) |
| failed | The ProductUsage record has been validated butrating failed |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The ExportJob task can be either:

- short-running task, where the result of the task can be returned in the same call to the client
- long-running task, where the result cannot be computed immediately; then the task resource can be created and returned to the client in the same API call

When an implementation for a Task supports both alternatives, it MAY decide at runtime to execute the task as short-running or long-running task, taking into consideration its expectation of the duration of task execution, e.g. by investigating any request parameters or payload values.

In that case, the consumer must be able to distinguish and handle both variants of the task operation.

Refer to TMF630 REST guidelines for more details on Task pattern.

## Information Framework

This Product Usage API manages an entity that is described in Information Framework (SID) in Product Usage ABE as ProductUsage entity.

These links permit to retrieve Information Framework documentation regarding Product Usage domain :

- Usage Specification : [https://www.tmforum.org/MODA/EARoot/EA4/EA2/EA4/EA6/](https://www.tmforum.org/MODA/EARoot/EA4/EA2/EA4/EA6/EA1712.htm) [EA1712.htm](https://www.tmforum.org/MODA/EARoot/EA4/EA2/EA4/EA6/EA1712.htm)
- Product Usage Part 1 : [https://www.tmforum.org/MODA/EARoot/EA4/EA2/EA4/EA6/](https://www.tmforum.org/MODA/EARoot/EA4/EA2/EA4/EA6/EA1716.htm) [EA1716.htm](https://www.tmforum.org/MODA/EARoot/EA4/EA2/EA4/EA6/EA1716.htm)
- Product Usage Part 2 : [https://www.tmforum.org/MODA/EARoot/EA4/EA2/EA4/EA6/](https://www.tmforum.org/MODA/EARoot/EA4/EA2/EA4/EA6/EA1718.htm) [EA1718.htm](https://www.tmforum.org/MODA/EARoot/EA4/EA2/EA4/EA6/EA1718.htm)

Information Framework excerpts:

Put simply, usage is how much service is used, by whom is it used, where and when is it used and circumstances under which it is used.

The ProductUsage describes the usage of an instantiated Product. Note that the API representation of Information Framework model is partial. In particular the direct relationship between a ProductUsage (that would be originated from a ResourceUsage) and a ResourceUsage is not implemented for now because of lack of business need for this.

Note that Information Framework and API specification may evolve independently but tend to be consistent as much as possible.

# Sample Use Cases 

The examples in this User Guide and OAS file come from the TMFS005 Use Case Billing Fiber Contract and TMFS009 Use Case Usage and Balance Management documents.

- Creation of a simple ProductUsage relating to a completed and rated voice call retrieval
- listing ProductUsage of usageType “InternationalVoice”
- retrieving a specific ProductUsage based on its id
- updating a Product Usage status to "recycled"

Note that entities and characteristic names don’t always fully match but the meaning should match.

## Export

Using ExportJob, the ProductUsage can be exported to a file.

Note : an implementation of this API could expose only exportJob resource if it’s agreed between API client and API server that the exportJob is the only way to retrieve ProductUsage (indivivual GET queries of productUsage not allowed). This can be useful for performance reasons, e.g. if the producUsage are of a high number and/or if the interface explicitely allows only 1 single mechanism to retrieve the productUsage entities for simplicity reasons.

# Support of polymorphism and extension patterns

Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by means of a list of generic meta-attributes that we describe below. Polymorphism in collections occurs when entities inherit from base entities, for instance a StringCharacteristic and BooleanCharacteristic inheriting properties from the abstract Characteristic entity.

Generic support of polymorphism and pattern extensions is described in the TMF API Guidelines, Part 2 (TMF630).

The @type attribute provides a way to represent the actual class type of an entity. For example, within a list of Characteristic instances some may be instances of StringCharacteristic where other could be instances of BooleanCharacteristic. The @type gives this information. All resources and sub-resources of the Product Usage API have a @type attributes that can be provided when this is useful.

The @referredType can be used within reference entities (like for instance a ProductUsageSpecificationtRef object) to explicitly denote the actual entity type of the referred class. Notice that in reference entities the @type, when used, denotes the class type of the reference itself, such as ProductUsageSpecificationtRef, and not the class type of the referred object. However since reference classes are rarely sub-classed, @type is generally not useful in reference objects.

The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined properties of an Entity or to specify the expected characteristics of an entity.

The @baseType attribute gives a way to provide explicitly the base of class of a given resource that has been extended.

### ExportJob resource

Represents a task used to export resources to a file.

### Resource model

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

_Figure 3 - ExportJob_

**Field descriptions**

**ExportJob fields**

| completionDate | A DateTime. Data at which the job was completed. |
| --- | --- |
| contentType | A String. The format of the exported data. This value should beaccording to the IANA standard list of media types. Default is'application/json'. |
| creationDate | A DateTime. Date at which the job was created. |
| errorLog | A String. Path to file or stream where errors encountered duringthe job processing can be written. |
| href | A String. Hyperlink reference. |
| id | A String. Unique identifier. |
| path | A String. A Json Pointer or a Json Path relative to the API rootnode that points to the resource acting as the source forstreaming content to the export destination specified by theExportJob. Defaults to the API?s root node. Using the JSONPointer resp. JSON Path with reference to the API rootguarantees that the path cannot point to a resource outside thescope of this API, e.g. to export some resource managed by adifferent API. |
| query | A String. Used to scope the exported data. Identical to GET filterconstruct using the API?s node defined by path as base.Defaults to requesting all resources of the node defined by thepath. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| status | A JobStateType. Valid values for the state of a batch job (e.g.catalog import). ENUMERATED with values:\* Not Started\* Running\* Succeeded\* Failed |
| --- | --- |
| url | A Uri. URL pointing at the location for the exported file. The URLsould be of the form [file://host/path ](file://host/path)where host is the fullyqualified domain name of the system on which the path isaccessible, and path is a hierarchical directory path of the formdirectory/directory/??/name. Other schemes can also besupported, e.g. 'ftp' and 'http', preferably with their TLS encryptedvariants 'sftp' resp 'https'. |
| @baseType | A String. When sub-classing, this defines the super-class. |
| @schemaLocation | A String. A URI to a JSON-Schema file that defines additionalattributes and relationships. |
| @type | A String. When sub-classing, this defines the sub-classExtensible name. |

## Notification Resource Models

3 notifications are defined for this API.

Notifications related to ExportJob:

- Create Event
- Delete Event
- State Change Event

The notification structure for all notifications in this API follow the pattern depicted by the figure below. A notification event resource (depicted by "SpecificEvent" placeholder) is a sub class of a generic Event structure containing at least an id of the event occurrence (eventId),

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

an event timestamp (eventTime), and the name of the resource (eventType). This notification structure owns an event payload structure ("SpecificEventPayload" placeholder) linked to the resource concerned by the notification using the resource name as access field ("resourceName" placeholder).

![](data:image/png;base64,)

# API OPERATIONS 

Remember the following Uniform Contract:

| Operation on Entities | Uniform API Operation | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Query Entities | GET Resource | GET must be used to retrieve arepresentation of a resource. |
| Create Entity | POST Resource | POST must be used to create anew resource |
| Partial Update of an Entity | PATCH Resource | PATCH must be used to partiallyupdate a resource |
| Remove an Entity | DELETE Resource | DELETE must be used toremove a resource |
| Execute an Action on an Entity | POST on TASK Resource | POST must be used to executeTask Resources |
| Other Request Methods | POST on TASK Resource | GET and POST must not beused to tunnel other requestmethods. |

Filtering and attribute selection rules are described in the TMF REST Design Guidelines.

Notifications are also described in a subsequent section.

### Updates partially a ProductUsage

```
PATCH /productUsage/{id}?fields=…
```

**Description**

This operation allows partial updates of a ProductUsage entity. Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) [html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub-resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

# API NOTIFICATIONS 

For every single of operation on the entities use the following templates and provide sample REST notification POST calls.

It is assumed that the Pub/Sub uses the Register and UnRegister mechanisms described in the REST Guidelines reproduced below.

## Register listener

**POST /hub**

**Description**

Sets the communication endpoint address the service instance must use to deliver information about its health state, execution state, failures and metrics. Subsequent POST calls will be rejected by the service if it does not support multiple listeners. In this case DELETE /api/hub/{id} must be called before an endpoint can be created again.

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 409 if request is not successful.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a request for registering a listener.

**Request**

```
POST /api/hub
Accept: application/json
{
    "callback": "http://in.listener.com"
}
```

**Response**

```
Content-Type: application/json
Location: /api/hub/42
{
    "id":"42",
    "callback": "http://in.listener.com",    "query":""
}
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Unregister listener

**DELETE /hub/{id}**

**Description**

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub..

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 404 if the resource is not found.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a request for un-registering a listener.

**Request**

```
DELETE /api/hub/42
Accept: application/json
```

**Response**

```
204
```

## Publish Event to listener

**POST /client/listener**

**Description**

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub.

Provides to a registered listener the description of the event that was raised. The /client/listener url is the callback url passed when registering the listener.

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 201 if the service is able to set the configuration.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a notification received by the listener. In this example “EVENT TYPE” should be replaced by one of the notification types supported by this API (see Notification resources Models section) and EVENT BODY refers to the data structure of the given notification type.

**Request**

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

```
POST /client/listener
Accept: application/json
{
    "event": {
        EVENT BODY    },
    "eventType": "EVENT_TYPE"
}
```

**Response**

```
201
```

For detailed examples on the general TM Forum notification mechanism, see the TMF REST Design Guidelines.

# Acknowledgements 

## Release Notes

### V4.0.0 vs v5.0.0

**general changes**

- common changes due to v5 tooling assets (OAS, User Guide, Conformance Profile…) generation
- usageSpecification endpoint removed, moved to TMF767 Product Usage Catalog Management API, same for usageSpecification related events
- endpoint /usage renamed into /productUsage. Note that serviceUsage and resourceUsage endpoints are managed in specific API TMF727 and TMF771
- usageXXX events removed (no more events)
- productUsage lifecycle changed to fit better the usage definition in Product domain
- addition of /exportJob resource to allow export of product usage data in a file, and exportJob events to receive corresponding notifications
- User Guide updated with excerpts from Information Framework and TMFS005 Use Case
- Conformance Profile updated accordingly to these changes

**schemas changes**

- productUsage : usageDate renamed into creationDate to follow general guidelines
- productUsage : lastUpdate added to have the latest update date of the product usage
- productUsage : externalIdentifier added to allow an array of external identifiers related to the product usage
- productUsage : status changed from enum to open string with enum proposal to allow more flexibility
- productUsage : usageCharacteristic uses generic Characteristic schema instead of UsageCharacteristic schema, to follow general guidelines
- productUsage : serviceUsage added to give the identifier of the service usage(s) that participated in the creation of the product usage
- productUsage : relatedParty uses RelatedPartyRefOrPartyRoleRef schema instead of RelatedParty schema to follow general guidelines
- productUsage : ratedProductUsage renamed into usageProductPrice to express this is a price
- productUsage : usageProductPrice uses common schema ProductPrice instead of RatedProductUsage schema
- productUsage : product reference is in the productUsage root instead of being in the usage price attribute for better clarity
- productUsage : usageSpecification uses ProductUsageSpecificationRef schema instead of UsageSpecificationRef schema, for better precision on the targetted schema

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- productUsage : usageSpecification, usageCharacteristic, product and usageProductPrice.productOfferingPrice are required for the ProductUsage\_FVO schema
